additional_source_authorization_checks.purpose: including shared report visibility after group/family revocation

checks: administrator uses an installed and verified globally published JDBC driver
administrator publishes reusable global connection rules in settings
publishing the inventory source shares the target without administrator credentials
administrators can publish an inventory target without configuring any database credentials
a newly invited user has no inherited administrator connections
mobile users explicitly confirm the target and test their own credentials
the saved inventory binding belongs only to the current user
JDBC SQL executes as the personal database principal and retains two workspace actions
ordinary users can add private configurations without publishing them globally
published revisions leave existing bindings unchanged until the user confirms and re-enters credentials
readonly users configure their own identity while platform write restrictions remain enforced
a second user and administrator cannot use another personal binding or private driver
real JDBC authentication failures provide safe categorized recovery guidance
failure diagnosis survives reload and fits the mobile connection card
credential recovery focuses an empty personal password field and clears stale failures
administrators inspect historical bindings and actual target differences across revisions
mobile users see their pinned revision and differences without management counts or controls
canceling a historical revision stop sends no mutation
a changed binding count rejects stale stop confirmation and refreshes the impact
confirmed stop blocks the historical personal bindings and preserves other revisions
reenabling a historical revision restores the original database identity without rebinding
administrators create a team and choose its real members in the browser
directory groups tags and maintainer contact are saved independently of target revisions
one publication supports both direct users and teams while hiding member details from consumers
directory management fits mobile and keeps its save action inside the viewport
mobile favorites are personal and recent use is based on a successful target connection
audit UI associates the platform actor personal database login driver and pinned revision
removing a team member revokes an existing connection and preserves a separate direct grant
team deletion requires an explicit impact confirmation and removes the owned fixture
revoking publication hides favorites and blocks a historical personal binding without deleting its credentials
desktop and mobile complete without browser page errors

limitations: commercial GaussDB and HA/distributed configurations unverified
openGauss TLS and non-PG modes unverified
no rerun of the full native version matrix
operation audit is best effort after request completion
organization tenants and shared query scheduling not implemented
